stories.title: BoJ to 1.25% (highest since 1995); DAX −0.5% near 26k as markets digest the hike

facts.text: Fri: Bank of Japan raised its policy rate from 1% to 1.25% (+25 bp) — highest since 1995; sixth hike since exiting negative rates in 2024 (BBC).
Move widely expected; BBC ties the global hiking wave to Iran-war energy prices after Wed’s Fed hike and the ECB’s earlier increase (BBC).
Japan core inflation eased to 1.7% in August from 1.8% — still near the BoJ’s 2% target (BBC).
tagesschau Marktbericht: DAX early trade −0.5% to 25,590 (Thu close 25,716 / +0.7%); buyers hesitant near 26,000 as all three major central banks sit on a tighter path (tagesschau).
tagesschau notes the BoJ hike “unter anderem wegen der Folgen des Iran-Kriegs”; German producer prices in August rose as strongly as in over three years (tagesschau).

stories.whyItMatters: Morning Asia open was “await BoJ” — lunch is the decision plus the European cash reaction.

stories.title: Putin puts Nestlé’s Russia business under forced administration

facts.text: Per decree, Russian assets of Nestlé were placed under forced administration by L.E.V. Management (tagesschau / ntv).
Nestlé said it takes note of the order, is reviewing options, and will take steps to protect its rights and keep operations running for employees (tagesschau).
Nestlé kept producing in Russia after the Ukraine invasion, citing essential food goods; ~6 factories, ~7,000 staff (2021), ~2% of group sales (tagesschau / ntv).
Same 2023 decree toolkit previously used on Danone, Carlsberg and Heineken — often a step before longer-term transfer to Kremlin-linked owners (tagesschau / ntv).

stories.whyItMatters: Another Western consumer name still operating in Russia is pulled into Moscow’s asset-control playbook — lunch wire, not in the morning brief.

stories.title: Wunstorf drone debris matches Leipzig model; federal prosecutors join probe

facts.text: NDR/security sources: crashed drone parts found near Fliegerhorst Wunstorf (Steinhuder Meer area) are the same model as the early-August Leipzig/Halle airport case (tagesschau/NDR).
Finder handed in a defective device early this week; police still searching the hard-to-access site for more fragments; no explosives traces reported so far (tagesschau / ntv).
Generalbundesanwalt has taken jurisdiction; BKA involved. ntv: GBA will look if a link to Leipzig “bestehen könnte”; build includes non-commercial / 3D-printed parts (ntv).
Wunstorf hosts Germany’s full A400M fleet — military airlift hub east of the find site (tagesschau / ntv).

stories.whyItMatters: Material update to morning’s Bonn/Leipzig thread — a second German site, same alleged design family, now at federal level.

stories.title: BDI lifts 2026 GDP call to +1.0% (from +0.6%); still no broad industrial upswing

facts.text: BDI now expects German GDP +1.0% in 2026, up from its prior +0.6% forecast (n-tv).

Hauptgeschäftsführerin Tanja Gönner: state spending on infrastructure and defence is driving growth while private investment stays weak — “von einem breiten industriellen Aufschwung könne noch keine Rede sein” (n-tv).
Research institutes had already raised 2026 expectations and remain more optimistic than the BDI’s new figure (n-tv).

stories.whyItMatters: Industry lobby soft-upgrade into Sunday’s state votes — fiscal/defence impulse, not a private-capex boom.

facts.text: Diesel ADAC all-time high: Thu avg €2.471/L (2nd daily record after Wed €2.453); Fri morning SWR ~€2.45/L; E10 eased to €2.308 (tagesschau).
Merz and Trump completed the phone call that was postponed last week (DLF).
Philippines: 16-year-old gunman kills two 14-year-old students, injures eight, then himself at Banga National High School (Mindanao) — third deadly school shooting since June (BBC).
Russia’s three-day State Duma vote opened in Kamchatka; opposition parties critical of the Ukraine war barred; United Russia win treated as locked-in (DLF).
